newsitem.title: GREECE: Forex inflows drive shorts down in late dealings.
newsitem.headline: Forex inflows drive shorts down in late dealings.

text.p: Renewed speculative forex inflows at the fixing put downward pressure on short rates, driving them 10 basis points lower for periods spanning one week to three months, dealers said.
The fall was more accentuated in one-week funds with longer tenors also easier.
"Speculative forex inflows to take advantage of rate differentials and the hard drachma policy drove short rates lower 10 basis points," said a trader at a state bank.
A dealer estimated 180 to 195 million ecus, $65-$67 million and 18-50 million marks were sold at the fixing for drachmas.
The central bank drained overnight money at an unchanged 12.40 percent.
The finance ministry is going to announce this week, possibly on Tuesday, the new committee for the management of public debt, government sources told Reuters.
Newly-elected Prime Minister Costas Simitis won a confidence vote in parliament on Sunday, calling on Greeks to tighten their belts to stay on course for EMU by the end of the century.
The mark was quoted at 156.53/56 drachmas from Monday's 156.585 fix, the dollar at 239.41/46 drachmas from 239.730 and the Ecu at 300.14/24 from 300.300 drachmas.
"The drachma has firmed vis-a-vis the ecu on the back of forex selling," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank.
